source_name: UniCredit Bank Hungary Zrt. – Befektetők / Kockázatkezelési (Pillar 3) jelentések
why_relevant: Long, uninterrupted series of Hungarian-language Pillar 3 'Kockázatkezelési jelentés' PDFs (2010 through recent years) plus the annual statutory accounts, hosted under /content/dam/cee2020-pws-hu/Rolunk/befektetok/. The PDF DAM path is stable and machine-friendly even though the navigation entry point is buried.

source_name: UniCredit Jelzálogbank Zrt. – Éves és gyorsjelentések
why_relevant: Mortgage-bank subsidiary reports filed under 'hasznos információk' (useful information) — an unusually low-visibility path that nonetheless holds statutory annual and flash reports and its own Pillar 3.

source_name: CIB Bank Zrt. – IFRS éves beszámolók (document/publications store)
why_relevant: Intesa Sanpaolo's Hungarian subsidiary publishes its separate and consolidated IFRS accounts as PDFs under year/announcement-structured document paths rather than a conventional IR page; this is the only entity-level CIB P&L.

source_name: CIB Bank – Jelentéseink (net.cib.hu CSR/sustainability report index)
why_relevant: GRI-standard sustainability/CSR reports on a separate host (net.cib.hu) from the main site; useful for non-financial and increasingly for CSRD/ESG disclosure tracking of an unlisted subsidiary.

source_name: KDB Bank Európa Zrt. – Pénzügyi adatok (IFRS statements + nyilvánosságra hozatal)
why_relevant: Small Korean-owned Hungarian bank; the single page carrying both its IFRS financial statements and its 'Kockázatokkal és tőkemegfeleléssel kapcsolatos nyilvánosságra hozatal' PDFs. Predictable PDF naming makes back-year collection easy.

source_name: Oberbank AG Magyarországi Fióktelep – Impresszum / Hitpt. 122.§ (4) b) közzétételek
why_relevant: As an EU branch (fióktelep), Oberbank HU has no separate Hungarian statutory accounts obligation of the Zrt. kind; its Hungarian estate is thin — an impresszum page carrying Hitpt. 122.§(4)b) publications and a list of MNB decisions back to 2015, plus a news page. Documents the shape of the branch-model disclosure gap.

source_name: Cofidis Magyarországi Fióktelepe – cofidis.hu dokumentumtár (üzletszabályzat, adatkezelés)
why_relevant: Consumer-credit branch of Cofidis SA. Searching found only dated business-rules and privacy PDFs under /media/ — no annual report or Pillar 3 page surfaced on the site. Still worth tracking: the versioned üzletszabályzat PDFs are a precise, dated record of product/pricing changes, and their absence of financials pins where the entity-level numbers must be sourced instead (e-beszámoló).

source_name: Elektronikus Beszámoló Portál (e-beszámoló, Igazságügyi Minisztérium) – Beszámoló keresés
why_relevant: The statutory deposit point for every Hungarian double-entry entity's annual accounts (mérleg, eredménykimutatás, kiegészítő melléklet, könyvvizsgálói jelentés). This is the authoritative fallback for entities whose own site publishes nothing — Cofidis, KDB, Oberbank branch — and the ground truth against which bank websites should be reconciled. Free, searchable by cégnév/adószám.

source_name: MNB Aranykönyv – felügyelt intézmények egyedi adatai (statisztika.mnb.hu)
why_relevant: Institution-by-institution balance sheet and P&L lines for every supervised Hungarian credit institution, as an interactive time series (2003 onwards) plus xlsx. For unlisted foreign-owned subsidiaries this is the cleanest structured, comparable entity-level dataset — no PDF parsing needed — and independently corroborates whatever the banks publish themselves.

source_name: Nemzeti Cégtár (nemzeticegtar.hu) – company records for HU bank entities and branches
why_relevant: Free-tier company register mirror giving cégjegyzékszám, registered seat, filing history and headline revenue for every entity in the cell — including the branches (fióktelep) that publish nothing themselves. Useful as the identity/alias resolver feeding e-beszámoló lookups.

source_name: OPTEN / Céginfo.hu – commercial credit-report providers for HU bank entities
why_relevant: Paid providers that normalise the deposited beszámoló data into structured, year-over-year financials (net revenue, headcount, filing dates) for all eight entities in the cell. Their free preview pages already expose headline revenue and are a fast triage layer; the paid feed is the pragmatic route if PDF parsing at scale is unattractive.

source_name: Magyar Bankszövetség – tagbanki adatlapok (member directory)
why_relevant: The Hungarian Banking Association member list is the cleanest authoritative actor map for the cell: official legal names, seats and links out to each member bank's site — the entry point for snowballing beyond the eight seeded institutions (e.g. other foreign-owned Zrt.s and fióktelep-model lenders).

source_name: Magyar Bankszövetség – Tagjaink (member institutions directory)
why_relevant: Curated register of ~67 Hungarian credit institutions, mortgage banks, guarantee funds plus associated members/observers (Társult tagok, Megfigyelők). Each entry links to a per-member detail page (tagreszlet.cshtml?tagId=N) carrying the institution's own site — the single best seed for enumerating every bank-level disclosure/IR source in HU.

source_name: Magyar Bankszövetség – Jelentések (annual and quarterly sector reports)
why_relevant: Association's own annual (évi beszámoló, 2001–2018 series) and quarterly (Q1–Q4 jelentés) sector reports plus 'Egyszerűsített Éves Beszámoló' 2023–2025, all as PDFs under /Public/jelentesek/. Gives sector-level narrative and aggregate banking results between MNB statistical releases.

source_name: Magyar Bankszövetség – Kommunikék (periodic sector communiqués)
why_relevant: Recurring communiqués summarising banking-sector developments and association positions; effectively the continuation channel for periodic sector commentary and the association's stance on regulation, fees and payments policy.

source_name: Magyar Bankszövetség – Sajtóközlemények (press releases)
why_relevant: Association press-release archive; fastest signal on sector-wide positions (interest-rate caps, transaction levy, instant payments, cash/ATM obligations) that precede individual bank disclosures.

source_name: Gazdaság és Pénzügy (G&P) – Bankszövetség academic journal
why_relevant: Peer-reviewed journal published by the association; carries data-rich articles on Hungarian bank profitability, digitalisation, payments and consolidation — often the only public quantitative treatment of niche topics (e.g. branch/ATM economics, cash logistics).

source_name: Magyar Bankszövetség – Munkacsoportok (working groups)
why_relevant: Working-group structure reveals which topics the sector is actively organising around (payments, digitalisation, compliance/AML, lending) and typically names the member banks and individuals leading each — a map of decision-makers and of live sector agenda items.

source_name: Hungarian Banking Association – English-language site
why_relevant: The .cshtml?lang=eng parameter serves an English mirror of the association pages, giving translated member names and report titles usable for cross-language entity resolution against EBF-level sources.

source_name: Magyar Fintech Szövetség (HFA) – Tagok (member companies)
why_relevant: The only curated register of the Hungarian fintech ecosystem (startups through mature vendors, incubators, accelerators). Founding/board members observed include Barion, Tőkeportál, BlockBen, Ergománia, Bankmonitor, BÁV Faktor, Blueopes, Flexibill, Péntech, TechTeamer. Seeds dozens of PSP/vendor sources no keyword search surfaces.

source_name: Magyar Fintech Szövetség – Riport (association reports / fintech ecosystem mapping)
why_relevant: Association-published reports and ecosystem maps of Hungarian fintech; the closest thing to a sector yearbook for non-bank payment and fintech players, which otherwise publish no consolidated results.

source_name: Budapest Fintech Week – conference programme and exhibitor/speaker list
why_relevant: The association's flagship annual event (next observed edition 1–4 December 2026) plus monthly Meetups and Business Breakfast Talks. Speaker/sponsor/exhibitor rosters are a live indicator of which vendors are actively selling into Hungarian banks — a competitor-detection channel that member lists lag behind.

source_name: Magyar Lízingszövetség – Lízingszövetségi statisztikák
why_relevant: Association-compiled leasing market statistics with an archive reported back to 2000, broken down by asset class (vehicles, real estate, equipment) and by member company. The authoritative HU leasing-volume series; ~36 member companies financing >HUF 1,300bn of assets.

source_name: Magyar Lízingszövetség – Éves beszámoló (annual report)
why_relevant: The leasing association's own annual report — sector narrative plus, typically, the member roster and full-year volumes. Companion channels: sajtóközlemény, tagi hírek (member news), infografikák.

source_name: Magyar Lízingszövetség – Tudásbázis (Eurotax reports, Datahouse data, ismertetők)
why_relevant: Knowledge base republishing third-party market datasets (Eurotax vehicle-valuation reports, Datahouse registration data) alongside the association's own explainers. A cheap route to commercial datasets that are otherwise paywalled at source.

source_name: GVH – Keresés versenyhivatali döntésekben (competition decision search)
why_relevant: Full-text searchable archive of Hungarian Competition Authority decisions covering 1997–2026, filterable by keyword, date range, decision number and party (eljárás alá vont). Bank/PSP merger clearances and consumer-protection cases contain market-share, pricing and product detail that appears in no other public source.

source_name: GVH – Összefonódások / Fúziók (merger control guidance and case practice)
why_relevant: Merger-control landing page for professional users; the entry point for tracking bank/leasing/PSP consolidation filings. Paired with GVH közlemények (e.g. 8/2017 as amended by 2/2018 and 3/2020 on conditions and obligations in non-prohibitive merger decisions), it explains how remedies are framed in HU banking deals.

source_name: GVH – Beszámoló az Országgyűlés részére (annual report to Parliament)
why_relevant: GVH's statutory annual report to Parliament reviews the year's cases sector by sector; historically includes banking-sector merger reviews (e.g. the 1997 Bank Austria/CA case). A compact retrospective index of competition activity in financial services.
